messages:
jamal: Heads-up — onboarding vanguard-8b today. License attached says 'must display attribution and upstream model link when offering as a service'. Also has a clause about 'no redistribution of weights in transformed form' — unsure if quantized weights count. cc @alexa for legal.
priya: Is this the FLOSS-style attribution or a more specific branding notice? Any exact wording we need in the Console UI/Docs?
alexa: I haven't seen the license text yet. Can you paste the exact clause? If it's an attribution clause it usually maps to our docs, but 'transformed form' language is tricky re: quantization.
jamal: Here's the snippet we got in the model bundle:

```
Redistribution prohibition: You may not redistribute the model weights or any derivative representations (including but not limited to quantized, pruned, or otherwise transformed weights) to third parties.
Attribution: If you offer services using this model, you must provide a visible attribution link to the upstream model and include the original authors in your docs/credits.
```

jamal: Also, quantized eval showed ~0.6% perplexity regression but identical classification F1 on our finetune subset. That aside — question is: can we run this on Redwood Dedicated/Private for paying customers? Or does 'redistribute' ban block hosting inference for customers in Dedicated where weights remain on our infra?
omar: From infra POV, Dedicated nodes run customer workloads on isolated pools. We never ship weights outside Redwood network. But some customers snapshot instances — policies allow them to export? Not by default. We need legal clarity for whether serving == redistribution.
alexa: Preliminary read: 'redistribute' typically means transferring copies to third parties. Hosting inference where weights remain on our servers is usually allowed. The clause specifically mentions "redistribute to third parties" — so Dedicated where customers don't get a copy should be OK. But the line "derivative representations (including quantized, pruned, or otherwise transformed weights)" worries me if we ever need to provide a quantized binary to a customer (e.g., to run in their VPC/offline).
priya: So for Private deployments (customer-managed on-prem) we *do* hand over model artifacts during install. That sounds blocked by this clause unless we negotiate. Any negotiation precedent?
alexa: We have a path: ask upstream for an addendum or commercial license that permits distribution to contractually-bound customers. For Private, we should treat model as 'not allowed' to ship until license exceptions are obtained. For Dedicated/Hosted, OK to serve.
jamal: Great. For documentation: what exact attribution phrasing is required? The clause says "visible attribution link to the upstream model and include the original authors in your docs/credits". Is a link in our Console credits + API docs sufficient, or must we show it in product UI where model selection happens?
alexa: Conservative approach: include a link in the model detail page in Console and in public docs that mention model provenance. Also add a small note in the SDK docs and the model metadata returned by our API (e.g., model.metadata.attribution_url). That should meet 'visible' requirement.
jamal: license-bot: run quick license scan? Can you add tags for 'no-redistribute', 'requires-attribution' to this model in onboarding sheet?
license-bot: scanning... done. Tags added: no-redistribute, requires-attribution, downstream-commercial-check.
priya: Action items: 1) legal to request addendum for Private distribution (alexa) 2) engineering to ensure attribution URL surfaces in Console + API (jamal/omar) 3) Product to update onboarding checklist and customer-facing docs (priya). I'll create a board ticket.
omar: On the quantization side: we should avoid distributing quantized artifacts to customers until addendum confirmed. For Dedicated, we can run quantized kernels on our servers; just don't expose weights.
jamal: Noted. Also flagging the ~0.6% perplexity regression for model quality team — want to run a focused eval suite (LLMsuite + our user prompts) before enabling default quantized runtime.
priya: I'll coordinate with QA/evals. Keeping this thread for legal sign-off and implementation notes. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
